title: The Other Screen
tagline: Steam only uses one of the Thor's two screens. I put the other to work.
what: A companion app for the bottom screen of the AYN Thor, a handheld with two screens. It watches what Steam is pointing at up top and shows what the top screen can't: achievements, play time, a keyboard, game controls.
built: Bottom screen follows Steam's focus: move along a row up top and that game's card appears below
A game card with Overview, Achievements and On this Thor pages you swipe between
Moved Steam's on-screen keyboard to the bottom, with Steam's own swipe typing
While a game runs: a taskbar, touch buttons, achievements and a performance page
credit: Remix of Barry Launcher by Project Barry

remix.changed: Kept its window, replaced everything it shows with my own skin and a background service that reads what Steam is focused on.

making.problem: The bottom screen sat there with the last game's art on it, telling me nothing the top screen didn't.
how: A small background service asks Steam what it is focused on and publishes it.
My skin for Barry Launcher draws the right thing for that focus: a game card, a post to read, a friend, a download, the clock.
Anything the top screen already shows gets dropped from the top or replaced with something only the Thor knows, like battery hours left for this game.

proof.caption: Moving along a row on top: the bottom shows that game's card. Top recorded on the Thor, bottom replayed from the data it was showing.
The Achievements page, swiped to. My real skin code on sample data, filmed off the device.
My own Library tab groups games by system, and the bottom shows that system's card. Top recorded on the Thor, bottom replayed.
Steam's keyboard moved to the bottom, with accents on a held key. My real skin code on sample data, filmed off the device.
